title: Stripe-aware segment packing, prefill throttling, and opportunistic KV repair
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Paged KV backends exhibit stripe-level fragmentation that increases memory amplification and degrades prefill performance during high-concurrency prefill bursts. Existing eviction heuristics are global-LRU and are blind to allocation stripe/segment layout, causing many small free segments that are expensive to coalesce during decode. Additionally, prefill bursts from concurrent requests overwhelm kernel selection and force suboptimal small-batch kernels, raising 95th percentile latency.

Goal: Implement a stripe-aware segment packing allocator plus prefill throttling and an opportunistic KV repair pass to reduce fragmentation, improve KV hit rate, and smooth prefill decode scheduling so we preserve low tail latency without sacrificing throughput. Target metrics: reduce memory fragmentation score by >=10% (measured by free-segment-count-weighted-by-size), increase end-to-end prefill KV hit rate by >=12%, and cut 95th decode latency for prefill-heavy workloads by >=15% in internal benchmarks.

Constraints: must be compatible with paged-attention layout, work across dedicated and hosted modes, incremental rollout with canary, and not require model changes. Implementation should be conservative by default and opt-in per-route via console config.

High-level approach: 1) Allocator: introduce stripe-aware segment packing where new allocations prefer contiguous segments in the same stripe and consolidate small frees into stripe-level free lists. This reduces cross-stripe fragmentation and lookup overhead. 2) Prefill throttling: implement a token-bucket-leveler per-GPU that detects prefill bursts and gates prefill tasks to keep batch sizes in the range that selects the preferred high-throughput kernels. 3) Opportunistic KV repair: background low-priority worker that scans hot shards during idle periods to coalesce small frees and optionally migrate short-lived entries into compacted segments. Repair runs are rate-limited and abortable. 4) Kernel hinting: expose hint metadata from allocator to kernel selector so it can prefer coplacement-friendly kernels when segments are packed.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but increases CPU and PCIe traffic; we propose a conservative default schedule with adaptive backoff tied to latency SLO. Throttling reduces immediate throughput but prevents pathological tail events; we will expose tunables to allow higher throughput at the cost of tail.
design_decisions: Prefer stripe-local free-lists to reduce cross-stripe compaction costs
Background repair should be low-priority and abortable when decode latency rises
Prefill throttling uses per-GPU token buckets with a fast path allowance for short-lived single-request bursts
Allocator emits lightweight placement hints to kernel selector instead of forcing kernel changes
Conservative defaults: features disabled for older runtimes; opt-in via route-level config before broad rollout

acceptance_criteria: Allocator passes unit and fuzz tests; no regressions in allocation correctness
Benchmarks show >=12% KV hit-rate improvement on prefill-heavy traces
95th percentile decode latency reduced by >=15% in internal canary cluster under target load
Background repair does not increase CPU utilization >5% over baseline during steady-state
Feature gated behind per-route opt-in; rollout playbook documented
Design doc and code reviewed with approvals from Runtime and Infra leads
End-to-end integration test added to CI (deterministic small-scale scenario)
